title: 150 Dishes for Four Lakh Guests at Anant Singh Daughter's Ladma Wedding
excerpt: Shivangi Singh's November 25 wedding in Ladma is being planned around a feast of about 150 dishes for roughly four lakh guests, a Defender reported as a gift for the groom, and a horse race with a Mahindra Thar as the prize.
body:
• Bihar MLA Anant Singh's younger daughter Shivangi Singh will marry Rishikesh Kumar in the family's ancestral village of Ladma on November 25, with catering being arranged for around four lakh guests.
  • Reports put the planned menu at about 150 dishes, mixing Bihari fare with sweets including Silav's khaja and kaju katli.
  • Singh is reported to be gifting his son-in-law a Land Rover Defender, with reports valuing it at roughly ₹2.5-3 crore.
  • A horse race is planned with a Mahindra Thar as the winner's prize and a motorcycle for the runner-up; the politicians and film stars named in reports are invitees, not confirmed attendees.

The wedding feast is the centrepiece. For the November 25 wedding of his younger daughter Shivangi Singh in Ladma village, Bihar MLA Anant Singh's family is arranging food for around four lakh guests, with a menu reported at about 150 dishes, according to India Today's reporting. Shivangi will marry Rishikesh Kumar, also known as Ankit, a resident of Krishnanagar in Patna's Bihta.

What is on the menu, as reported

The spread is reported to combine traditional Bihari dishes with well-known sweets. Report Wire said the roughly 150 items will include Silav's khaja and kaju katli alongside Bihari fare. No fuller dish-by-dish menu has been published in the reports read for this article, so the feast is best understood by its scale — catering for roughly four lakh people — rather than by an itemised list.

The same day carries a second family ceremony: the sacred-thread initiation of Singh's younger son, Abhinav, according to India Today. That is part of why the catering operation is so large.

"Singh is reported to be gifting his son-in-law a Land Rover Defender, with reports valuing it at roughly ₹2.5-3 crore."

The gifts and the horse race

Report Wire reported that Singh intends to present his son-in-law, Rishikesh Kumar, with a Land Rover Defender, described as a top-variant model valued at roughly ₹2.5-3 crore and said to have already arrived in Patna. The value is a reported figure, not a confirmed price.

A horse race is planned as part of the celebrations, with horses being brought from across the country. The winner will receive a Mahindra Thar and the runner-up a motorcycle, Singh said, according to India Today. There will be no firecrackers, Singh said, citing environmental concerns. One report also carried a rumour that models from Dubai would be flown in for the reception; that detail is unconfirmed and is not presented here as part of the confirmed programme.

Who has been invited — not who has confirmed

Invitations are not attendance. India Today reported that Singh plans to invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and that former Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar, RJD chief Lalu Prasad Yadav and Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav are on the list. Actor Sonu Sood, folk singer Maithili Thakur, MP and singer Manoj Tiwari, Bhojpuri star Pawan Singh and actor Akshara Singh have been invited, Singh said — with their attendance yet to be confirmed. The World Opinion's report listed further entertainment names as reportedly invited, including Amrapali Dubey, Ravi Kishan and Udit Narayan; those names are reported invitations only.

The setting

Preparations stretch across several acres in Ladma, with land readied for pandals and a horse-racing ground and decorators brought in from Mau in Uttar Pradesh, according to India Today. For readers who know Bihar's big wedding season, the story is the scale of the kitchen as much as the guest list: a single-family celebration planning to feed a crowd the size of a small city, built around regional dishes and sweets rather than a published banquet menu.
nri_angle: The feast — 150 dishes built around Bihari fare and sweets like Silav khaja for a crowd of four lakh — is a window on the scale of Bihar's wedding-season food culture for diaspora readers with roots in the state.
author: Diaspora Desk
